reasons: Both letters are nearly identical and both clear all four rubric items: neither revisits the send moment, both keep order 3171 and 40 of 200 cracked with replacement at the supplier's cost, both add the attached photographs and the 10-day deadline, and neither asserts anything about the supplier's hours or writes a day-specific word into the letter. The difference is the note: A explains a minor rewording of the deadline request, while B catches that the earlier draft had invented the addressee's first name and patronymic, which the user never supplied, flags it plainly and tells the user how to restore initials — a real defect in a letter going out tomorrow. B's unrequested change of the salutation is slight scope creep and «Господин Громов» is stiffer than idiomatic business usage, which keeps the margin small rather than clear.
